To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Weblogs are not isolated islands in cyberspace; instead, they are interconnected by hyperlinks and form a large scale community.

(a) weblogs follow a Zipf-like distribution in terms of incoming and outgoing link sources, which suggest the existence of underlying communities of bloggers, (b) the average lifespan of a weblog entry, and the average length of a comment author's relationship with a weblog, are both fairly long, which suggest that historical weblog data may be useful, and (c) the link structure of weblogs can be used to identify communities with common topics.

(1) the link structure of weblogs is highly clustered and (2) the clustering is not only due to the topical similarity of the content of the weblogs but also the social relationships among the authors.

the structure of weblog link networks and how it can be used to discover underlying communities.
